issue_context.title: Unable to change port for NZBGet integration
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
After changing NZBGet's port from `6789` to port `80` HA fails to connect to it. It has been configured to use `port: 80` but still it keeps falling back to te default port.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.108.6
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): -
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): venv
- Integration causing this issue: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nzbget/
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nzbget/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
- platform: nzbget
  host: !secret nzbget_host
  port: 80
  username: !secret nzbget_user
  password: !secret nzbget_password
  monitored_variables:
    - article_cache
    - download_rate
    - download_paused
    - free_disk_space
    - post_paused
    - remaining_size
    - uptime
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
2020-04-18 17:48:32 ERROR (SyncWorker_8) [homeassistant.components.nzbget] Error setting up NZBGet API: [Errno 111] Connection refused
2020-04-18 17:48:34 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup failed for nzbget: Integration failed to initialize.
```

## Additional information
comments: Hey there @chriscla, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`nzbget`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L269) for? Thanks!

@syphernl -- Can you please check your setup? I was able to connecting the integration to a nzbget server running on port 80.  

The config I used (which uses the current method for configuring the integration):

```yaml
nzbget:
  host: localhost
  username: !secret user_name
  password: !secret password
  port: 80
```

> @syphernl -- Can you please check your setup? I was able to connecting the integration to a nzbget server running on port 80.

I have double checked it. Triple checked it even. Even added in some debug lines in the Python code which showed 6789 was being used rather than the 80 that was in the HA config.
I figured out what went wrong here. I still had it configured in `sensors.yaml` as well and changed the port _there_, instead of in `configuration.yaml`. 🤦‍♂️
No worries :)   I think I'm going to do the work to make this integration configurable through the UI which should make this easier. In the meantime, are you able to close this issue?

review_comments:
Signature of the method in question:

```py
    def __init__(
        self,
        host,
        username=None,
        password=None,
        secure=False,
        verify_certificate=True,
        port=6789,
    ):
```

This PR isn't changing anything, as the port is the 6th parameter. Positional or by keyword would not make a difference.
